title: Bacteria, viruses, fungi and protists: four kinds of pathogen
examples: What are the four types of pathogen?
Is malaria caused by a virus?
What is the difference between bacteria and viruses?

figure.name: x-sort
figure.question: Which kind of pathogen causes it?

explain.say: Have you ever had a cold, a tummy bug or itchy feet? Each was caused by a pathogen, a tiny living thing, or particle, that causes disease. There are four main kinds. Let's sort some famous diseases into their groups.

draw.text: Bacteria, viruses, fungi and protists: four kinds of pathogen

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Which kind of pathogen causes it?

explain.say: Look at the first group: bacteria. They are single cells, much smaller than yours, and some make poisons called toxins. Cholera spreads in dirty water; tuberculosis spreads through coughs. Which medicine kills bacteria, do you think?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Which kind of pathogen causes it?

explain.say: Now the viruses. They are far smaller than bacteria and are not even cells. A virus gets inside your cells and makes them build more viruses. Flu, measles and COVID-19 are viruses. Do antibiotics work on viruses?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Which kind of pathogen causes it?

explain.say: See the fungi group? Some fungi grow on skin, like athlete's foot and ringworm, or on plants, like black spot on roses. Then the protists: malaria is caused by a protist carried by mosquitoes. Which one surprised you?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Which kind of pathogen causes it?

explain.say: So: bacteria, viruses, fungi and protists. Brilliant sorting! Wow fact: malaria still affects over 200 million people a year, which is why mosquito nets save so many lives.

faq.q: How do bacteria make us ill?
faq.a: Bacteria multiply quickly inside the body, and many release toxins that damage tissues and make us feel ill. Antibiotics can kill most bacteria.

faq.q: What is the difference between bacteria and viruses?
faq.a: Bacteria are living cells that can reproduce on their own and can be killed by antibiotics. Viruses are much smaller, are not cells, can only reproduce inside other cells, and are not affected by antibiotics.
Fungi cause athlete's foot and ringworm on human skin, and diseases in plants like rose black spot and wheat rust. They are treated with antifungal medicines.

faq.q: Is malaria caused by a virus?
faq.a: No. Malaria is caused by Plasmodium, a single-celled protist. It is spread by the bite of female Anopheles mosquitoes.
Through the air in droplets from coughs and sneezes, in dirty water or food, by direct contact, and by animals called vectors, such as mosquitoes.

facts: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium protists and is spread by female Anopheles mosquitoes.
Antibiotics kill bacteria but have no effect on viruses.
The WHO estimated about 249 million malaria cases worldwide in 2022.

quiz.show: Which disease is caused by a protist?
